title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: Supply data frame element symbols numeric column. ggPSE() maps column fill gradient returns standard ggplot2 object.  Elements data appear neutral grey. result plain ggplot2 object, can keep adding layers:
code: battery <- data.frame(   symbol     = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P", "C"),   importance = c(0.95, 0.88, 0.75, 0.60, 0.45, 0.40, 0.35) ) ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance", legend_title = "Battery relevance") ggPSE(battery,       value_col    = "importance",       color_low    = "#f7fbff",       color_high   = "#08519c",       legend_title = "Battery relevance") +   labs(title = "Critical elements for Li-ion batteries") +   theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: Use groups, periods, lanthanides, actinides display portion periodic table.
code: # Transition metals only ggPSE(battery,       value_col   = "importance",       groups      = c(3, 12),       periods     = c(4, 6),       lanthanides = FALSE,       actinides   = FALSE,       legend_title = "Battery relevance") # Full table without lanthanides and actinides ggPSE(battery,       value_col   = "importance",       lanthanides = FALSE,       actinides   = FALSE,       legend_title = "Battery relevance")

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: highlight parameter colors groups elements adds legend entry group.
code: ggPSE(highlight = list(   list(symbols = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P"),        color   = "#2166ac",        label   = "Battery metals"),   list(symbols = c("Nd", "Dy", "Tb", "Pr", "La", "Ce"),        color   = "#e63946",        label   = "Rare earth magnets") ))

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE_bubble() maps numeric column bubble size clean white background.
code: supply_risk <- data.frame(   symbol = c("Li", "Co", "Nd", "Dy", "Pt", "Rh", "In", "Ga"),   risk   = c(0.62, 0.91, 0.84, 0.88, 0.52, 0.70, 0.78, 0.65) ) ggPSE_bubble(supply_risk, size_col = "risk",              bubble_color = "#d73027", legend_title = "Supply risk score")

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE_bar() draws proportional bar inside tile growing chosen edge.
code: ggPSE_bar(supply_risk, value_col = "risk",           bar_side     = "bottom",           bar_color    = "#2166ac",           legend_title = "Supply risk score") #> Warning: ggPSE_bar() draws no legend; 'legend_title' is ignored.

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE_donut() draws small donut pie chart inside tile showing categorical breakdown — example supply mix country phase composition. Requires ggforce package.  Combine gradient fill encode two variables simultaneously:
code: supply <- data.frame(   symbol   = c("Li","Li","Li", "Co","Co", "Nd","Nd", "Pt"),   category = c("CL","AU","AR", "CD","AU", "CN","RU", "ZA"),   share    = c(0.60, 0.30, 0.10, 0.70, 0.30, 0.80, 0.20, 1.00) )  ggPSE() |>   ggPSE_donut(supply, category_col = "category", share_col = "share",               legend_title = "Producer") # Note: combining gradient fill with donut charts requires ggnewscale # to avoid scale conflicts - planned for a future release criticality <- data.frame(   symbol = c("Li", "Co", "Nd", "Pt"),   value  = c(0.70, 0.91, 0.85, 0.60) ) ggPSE(criticality, value_col = "value", legend_title = "Criticality") |>   ggPSE_donut(supply, category_col = "category", share_col = "share",               legend_title = "Producer")

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE_profile() extracts single period, group, f-block row combines line plot numeric property. Requires patchwork.
code: data(ggpse_elements) ggPSE_profile(ggpse_elements, value_col = "electronegativity", period = 2) ggPSE_profile(ggpse_elements, value_col = "atomic_radius_pm", group = 1) ggPSE_profile(ggpse_elements, value_col = "electronegativity",               lanthanides = TRUE)

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE_badge() overlays country flags (via optional ggflags package) ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 text codes. Multiple countries per element supported — three flags per tile.  Use hierarchy = TRUE scale flags importance order show_legend = TRUE append country legend. Requires patchwork.  Install ggflags flag icons:
code: supply_single <- data.frame(   symbol  = c("Li", "Co", "Nd", "Pt", "Cu", "Ni", "Ga", "In"),   country = c("CL", "CD", "CN", "ZA", "CL", "PH", "CN", "CN"),   value   = c(0.70, 0.91, 0.85, 0.60, 0.50, 0.55, 0.80, 0.75) ) ggPSE(supply_single, value_col = "value",       color_high = "#b2182b", legend_title = "Criticality") |>   ggPSE_badge(supply_single, country_col = "country") supply_multi <- data.frame(   symbol  = c("Li","Li","Li", "Co","Co", "Nd","Nd"),   country = c("CL","AU","AR", "CD","AU", "CN","RU"),   value   = c(0.70, 0.70, 0.70, 0.91, 0.91, 0.85, 0.85) ) ggPSE(supply_multi, value_col = "value", legend_title = "Criticality") |>   ggPSE_badge(supply_multi, country_col = "country",               hierarchy = TRUE, show_legend = TRUE) remotes::install_github("rensa/ggflags")

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE_theme() applies pre-built visual theme ggPSE plot.
code: ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance") |>   ggPSE_theme("minimal") ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance") |>   ggPSE_theme("publication") ggPSE() |> ggPSE_theme("crazy", seed = 42)

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE_interactive() adds hover tooltips via ggiraph package. Renders HTML documents, Shiny apps, RStudio Viewer.
code: data(ggpse_elements) ggPSE_interactive(   ggpse_elements,   value_col    = "electronegativity",   tooltip_cols = c("name", "atomic_weight", "block", "electronegativity"),   legend_title = "Electronegativity (Pauling)" )

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE ships ggpse_elements, data frame 17 physical chemical properties 118 elements sourced IUPAC 2021 NIST WebBook.
code: data(ggpse_elements) ggPSE(ggpse_elements, value_col = "electronegativity",       color_low    = "#f7f7f7",       color_high   = "#d73027",       legend_title = "Electronegativity (Pauling)") ggPSE(ggpse_elements, value_col = "melting_point_K",       color_high   = "#08519c",       legend_title = "Melting point (K)")

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: Use ggPSE_save() sensible periodic table defaults, ggsave() directly full control.
code: p <- ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance")  # Convenience wrapper with PSE-optimised defaults ggPSE_save(p, "battery.png") ggPSE_save(p, "battery.pdf")  # Full control with ggsave ggsave("battery.png", p, width = 18, height = 8, units = "cm", dpi = 300) ggsave("battery.svg", p, width = 18, height = 8, units = "cm")

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: ggPSE_interactive() wraps standard ggPSE() output ggiraph interactivity. Every tile becomes hoverable, showing configurable tooltip element details. vignette shows use Quarto HTML document.

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
code: # Install ggPSE remotes::install_github("VJGeiger/ggPSE")  # Install ggiraph (required for interactivity) install.packages("ggiraph")

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: simplest call mirrors ggPSE() — pass data frame value column. Hovering tile shows element symbol, atomic number, value.
code: library(ggPSE)  battery <- data.frame(   symbol     = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P", "C"),   importance = c(0.95, 0.88, 0.75, 0.60, 0.45, 0.40, 0.35) )  ggPSE_interactive(battery,                   value_col    = "importance",                   legend_title = "Battery relevance")

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: Use tooltip_cols control appears hover tooltip. column present data frame can included.
code: data(ggpse_elements)  ggPSE_interactive(   ggpse_elements,   value_col    = "electronegativity",   tooltip_cols = c("name", "atomic_weight", "block",                    "electronegativity", "ionization_energy_eV"),   legend_title = "Electronegativity (Pauling)" )

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: ggPSE_interactive() supports highlight parameter ggPSE(). Hover still works tiles including highlighted ones.
code: ggPSE_interactive(   highlight = list(     list(symbols = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P"),          color   = "#2166ac",          label   = "Battery metals"),     list(symbols = c("Nd", "Dy", "Tb", "Pr", "La", "Ce"),          color   = "#e63946",          label   = "Rare earth magnets")   ) )

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: groups, periods, lanthanides, actinides parameters work exactly ggPSE(). , transition metals shown.
code: ggPSE_interactive(   ggpse_elements,   value_col   = "melting_point_K",   groups      = c(3, 12),   periods     = c(4, 6),   lanthanides = FALSE,   actinides   = FALSE,   legend_title = "Melting point (K)" )

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: Control hover fill color tooltip styling via hover_fill hover_stroke.
code: ggPSE_interactive(   battery,   value_col    = "importance",   hover_fill   = "#2166ac",   hover_stroke = "#ffffff",   legend_title = "Battery relevance" )

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: Adjust width_svg height_svg (inches) fit document layout.
code: ggPSE_interactive(   battery,   value_col  = "importance",   width_svg  = 10,   height_svg = 4 )

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: Works format: html . PDF Word output, use ggPSE() instead wrap chunk #| eval: !knitr::is_latex_output(). Shiny, use ggiraph::girafeOutput() ggiraph::renderGirafe() instead calling ggPSE_interactive() directly render function. interactive output embedded GitHub README directly. Use GIF README link hosted HTML version via GitHub Pages.

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
code: library(shiny) library(ggPSE) library(ggiraph)  ui <- fluidPage(   titlePanel("Interactive Periodic Table"),   sidebarLayout(     sidebarPanel(       selectInput("prop", "Property",                   choices = c("electronegativity", "melting_point_K",                               "density_g_cm3", "ionization_energy_eV"))     ),     mainPanel(       girafeOutput("pse", width = "100%", height = "500px")     )   ) )  server <- function(input, output) {   output$pse <- renderGirafe({     data(ggpse_elements)     ggPSE_interactive(       ggpse_elements,       value_col    = input$prop,       tooltip_cols = c("name", "atomic_weight", input$prop),       legend_title = input$prop     )   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: ggPSE — Periodic Table Visualization
text: Map numeric variable fill color gradient across elements.  mapping can also applied selection PSE.  also possible customize ggplots multigradient scales better visualization.
code: battery <- data.frame(   symbol     = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P", "C"),   importance = c(0.95, 0.88, 0.75, 0.60, 0.45, 0.40, 0.35) )  ggPSE(battery,       value_col    = "importance",       color_low    = "#f7fbff",       color_high   = "#08306b",       legend_title = "Battery relevance") data(ggpse_elements) ggPSE(ggpse_elements[ggpse_elements$block == "d", ],       value_col = "density_g_cm3", legend_title = "Density (g/cm3)") data(ggpse_elements)  ggPSE(ggpse_elements,       value_col    = "density_g_cm3",       color_low    = "#2166ac",          color_high   = "#a50026",          legend_title = "Density (g/cm³)") +   ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn(     colours  = c("#2166ac", "#1a9850", "#a50026"),     na.value = "#f0f0f0",     name     = "Density (g/cm³)"   ) +   ggplot2::labs(title = "Elemental density across the periodic table") +   ggplot2::theme(plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))

title: Plot a periodic table with a continuous value overlay — ggPSE
text: data data frame element symbols (case-sensitive, e.g. "Cl") value column. Rows may repeat element (e.g. one row per country) long agree value; different values element, unknown NA symbols non-numeric values give error. NULL, blank table using NA color drawn. value_col Character. Column name data map fill color. symbol_col Character. Column data containing element symbols. Default "symbol". label_value Logical. Print numeric values inside tiles. Default TRUE. value_digits Integer. Decimal places displayed values. Default 2. color_low Hex color low end gradient. Default "#fdf0f2". color_high Hex color high end gradient. Default "#9a031e". color_na Hex color elements data. Default "#f0f0f0". tile_border Color tile borders. NULL (default) border drawn ("transparent"). Set color "white" "grey30" draw borders. highlight Elements colour category. Either named list symbol vectors, e.g.     list("Alkali metals" = c("Li", "Na", "K"), Halogens = c("F", "Cl")).     names become legend labels list order legend     order. split(df$symbol, df$category) gives list; use     factor category control order. Colours come     highlight_colors. list groups, list     symbols (character vector element symbols), color     (fill color) optional label (legend label), e.g.     list(list(symbols = c("Li","Co"), color = "#2166ac",     label = "Battery metals")). Unknown symbols elements listed one group give warning (case last group wins). legend_title Character. Legend title. Defaults value_col; highlight groups title unless set one. show_atomic_number Logical. Show atomic numbers inside tile. Default FALSE. See number_position drawn. base_size Numeric. Base font size pt. Default 10. groups Integer vector length 2. Range IUPAC groups (columns) display, e.g. c(3, 12) transition metals . Default NULL shows groups. periods Integer vector length 2. Range periods (rows 1-7) display, e.g. c(4, 6) periods 4 6. Default NULL shows periods. Note: lanthanides actinides controlled separately via lanthanides actinides. lanthanides Logical. Show lanthanide row. Default TRUE. actinides Logical. Show actinide row. Default TRUE. symbol_position element symbol drawn inside tile: "center" (default), "top", "bottom", "left" "right". value label shown (label_value = TRUE), placed opposite side "top" / "bottom", stacked symbol "left" / "right". number_position atomic number drawn show_atomic_number = TRUE: "top-left" (default), "top", "top-right", "left", "right", "bottom-left", "bottom" "bottom-right". warning given overlaps symbol value text. symbol_size Size element symbol ggplot2 text units (mm, size argument geom_text()). Default NULL scales base_size (base_size * 0.4). symbol affected; value atomic number keep scaling base_size. Large symbols need room, see symbol_position. label_na Logical. Draw symbols (atomic numbers / values) tiles without data? Default TRUE. FALSE, tiles value (part highlight group) stay blank, useful subset elements covered data. Ignored neither value_col highlight given. text_color single colour used tile text instead automatic black/white contrast colour. Default NULL. Useful fill scale replaced afterwards (e.g. scale_fill_gradient2()), automatic colour derived color_low / color_high. symbol_nudge, number_nudge Numeric. Vertical shift symbol / atomic number tile units (tile 0.92 high; positive moves ), added position set symbol_position / number_position. Default 0. value label moved, overlap warning take nudge account. highlight_colors Colours named-list highlight: either vector named group (order matter, extra names ignored) unnamed vector matched position. R colour accepted. Default NULL uses colour-blind-safe palette (Okabe-Ito, extended beyond 8 groups). Ignored, warning, groups carry color.

code: battery <- data.frame(   symbol     = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe"),   importance = c(0.95, 0.88, 0.75, 0.60, 0.45) ) ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance", legend_title = "Battery relevance")   ggPSE(highlight = list(   list(symbols = c("Li", "Co", "Ni"), color = "#2166ac", label = "Battery"),   list(symbols = c("Nd", "Dy", "Tb"), color = "#e63946", label = "Magnets") ))   # Categories from a named list, with your own colours ggPSE(highlight = list(Alkali = c("Li", "Na", "K"), Halogens = c("F", "Cl", "Br")),       highlight_colors = c(Alkali = "firebrick", Halogens = "steelblue"),       legend_title = "Group")   # Show only transition metals (groups 3-12, periods 4-6) ggPSE(groups = c(3, 12), periods = c(4, 6), lanthanides = FALSE, actinides = FALSE)   # Symbol at the top, atomic number in the bottom-right corner ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance",       symbol_position = "top", show_atomic_number = TRUE,       number_position = "bottom-right") #> Warning: number_position = "bottom-right" overlaps with the symbol or value text when symbol_position = "top"; choose another number_position.   # Smaller symbols independent of base_size ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance", symbol_size = 3)   # Only label the elements that have data, with one fixed text colour ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance", label_na = FALSE, text_color = "grey15")   # Fine-tune: symbol slightly above its position ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance", symbol_position = "top",       symbol_nudge = 0.05)

"dark" Dark background, dark tile borders, light legend     text. Tiles without data symbol colours keep light-theme     look, starting point rather finished dark mode. "publication" print: solid white background, thin     dark-grey tile borders (light empty tiles stay visible print     greyscale; tile_border set kept),     white tiles elements without data (mistaken     lowest values black white; color_na set     kept), compact legend fixed small type (8 pt title, 7 pt labels), small     margins plain left-aligned title, subtitle caption styles.     Meant figures 18 cm (double column). narrower     figure use smaller base_size [ggPSE()] shorten     legend bar, e.g. + theme(legend.key.width = unit(0.7, "cm"))     8.5 cm. "crazy" Randomly assigns unique color tile.     call produces different result. seed Integer. Random seed "crazy" theme reproducibility. Default NULL gives different result call.

text: themes complete ggplot2 themes replace earlier theme() settings plot. Apply theme first, add tweaks: ggPSE(...) |> ggPSE_theme("publication") + theme(legend.position = "none"). plot pass modified. Note highlight plots, may want adjust highlight colors manually suit background.

title: Apply a pre-built theme to a periodic table plot — ggPSE_theme
code: data(ggpse_elements) p <- ggPSE(ggpse_elements, value_col = "electronegativity",            label_value = FALSE, legend_title = "Electronegativity")  p |> ggPSE_theme("minimal")  p |> ggPSE_theme("publication")  p |> ggPSE_theme("dark")   # Crazy: different every time, or reproducible with a seed ggPSE() |> ggPSE_theme("crazy", seed = 42)

title: ggPSE 0.3.0
text: New symbol_position argument ggPSE() ggPSE_interactive() draw element symbol "center" (default), "top", "bottom", "left" "right" tile. New number_position argument place atomic number eight border positions tile (default "top-left"). New symbol_size argument set symbol size independently base_size. New ggPSE_text() adds line text per tile data column (positions "top", "center", "bottom", plus fine-tuning position_nudge). Call ggPSE_donut(), removes text layers. New symbol_nudge number_nudge arguments shift symbol / atomic number vertically *_position. New label_na argument (hide symbols tiles without data) text_color (one fixed text colour instead automatic contrast colour) ggPSE() ggPSE_interactive(). highlight now also accepts named list symbol vectors, e.g. highlight = split(df$symbol, df$category), new highlight_colors argument (named position). legend_title now labels highlight legend. ggPSE_theme() longer removes colour scales ("minimal", "publication" "dark" used replace gradients highlight colours ggplot2’s defaults turn symbols salmon). "crazy" replaces fills. plot pass longer modified, docs examples now use ggPSE(...) |> ggPSE_theme("publication"). Redesigned "publication" theme print: white background, thin dark-grey tile borders, white tiles elements without data, compact legend fits, plain title, subtitle caption styles. Data given ggPSE(), ggPSE_interactive(), ggPSE_bubble(), ggPSE_bar() ggPSE_profile() checked: symbols element symbols (typos, lower case, stray spaces, element names, NA) now error names instead leaving tile silently blank, non-numeric -NA value columns. Repeated rows element allowed agree (e.g. one row per country), different values element error. ggPSE_badge(), ggPSE_donut() ggPSE_text() check symbols . Unknown symbols highlight error. value column named atomic_number, col row longer clashes internal tile table (used give blank plot error; ggPSE_interactive() silently used tile positions instead values). ggPSE_bubble() without size_col draws blank table instead failing. README: fixed typos gPSE_donut ggpse_elemts. ggPSE_bar(): bars now start zero default, length proportional value; , smallest value got bar constant values gave NaN. New limits argument; limits = range(x) gives previous scaling. legend_title never used (bars legend) now warns set. changes look existing bar plots. element tables lazy-loaded (LazyData: true): ggpse_elements ggpse_grid available library(ggPSE) without data(), hard-coded copy tile table inside package gone. ggPSE_badge(): badge_size multiplied 0.22 ggflags installed; unknown country code shown given instead NA legend; elements 3 countries rows without country code (e.g. Namibia’s "NA" read read.csv()) now give warning. ggPSE_profile() gives clear error period group single number. Documentation: tile_border longer claims detect background. Colours: ggPSE() ggPSE_interactive() new arguments colors (two colours), midpoint (diverging scales), limits (fixed colour range, e.g. frames animation), breaks labels, fill scale longer replaced afterwards. text colour tile now chosen colour tile really gets (estimated color_low/color_high range call, changed frame frame, used wrong colour space gave tiles without data mid-gradient colour). Fills unchanged; default gradient symbol colour changes tiles wrong (4 87 electronegativity example). text_color can now name column data one colour per element. Text layout now defined one internal helper shared ggPSE() ggPSE_interactive(). Documentation fix: base_size default 10, 8.
